# SCI-NOI v0.1 — Scientific-Owner ODQ-110A Approval

Decision identity: `SCI-NOI-ODQ-110A`

Scientific owner: Grant Wilson

Decision date: `2026-08-29`

Status: approved external transformation ownership and exact realization-parity
policy

## Exact Owner Decision

NOI does not choose or define a deterministic filter or other scientific
transformation. The appropriate upstream or downstream scientific process owns
the transformation and defines the transformed scientific product. When NOI
estimates uncertainty for that transformed product, it must apply exactly the
owner-defined transformation to every admitted compatible randomization.

## Ownership Boundary

The transformation-owning process owns its scientific purpose, algorithm,
operator identity, parameters and learned state, application domain, support
and edge rules, normalization, units, response/transfer interpretation,
validity, lifecycle, and failure semantics. NOI shall not select, tune,
regularize, replace, simplify, or scientifically reinterpret that
transformation.

NOI owns only the realization-ensemble and uncertainty-method identity, exact
binding to the externally owned transformation, conforming application of that
transformation to admitted randomizations, and truthful uncertainty-product
scope and limitations. Invoking the transformation through its owning process
or applying a content-bound equivalent representation does not transfer
scientific ownership to NOI.

## Exact-Parity Requirement

For a fixed-state transformed-product uncertainty method, the transformation
applied to every admitted randomization is exactly the transformation that
defines the immutable scientific product whose uncertainty is being estimated.
The method binds the transformation owner and exact version/generation,
operator and learned-state identity, parameters, insertion point and operation
order, parent, domain, units, normalization, support, boundary and edge
behavior, missing-data behavior, response/transfer state, lifecycle, and
failure policy.

No commutation, relocation, approximate substitution, parameter inference, or
same-name equivalence is implicit. Failure to establish exact identity and
parity makes that transformed-product uncertainty route unavailable; NOI must
not silently omit or replace the transformation.

If the transformation is rerun or relearned separately for realizations, that
is a distinct method under ODQ-104 rather than the fixed-state method approved
here. The scientifically consequential rerun/relearned stages and resulting
member-specific state must then be named explicitly.

## Product And Claim Boundary

The resulting empirical uncertainty applies only to the exact transformed
scientific product and domain. It cannot be attached to an untransformed or
differently transformed MAP, JINC, or other product by analogy. Applying the
same transformation to randomizations does not by itself establish source
cancellation, physical-noise equivalence, covariance completeness, calibrated
significance, or scientific validity of the transformation.

This approval does not define or admit a numerical filter, transformation, or
transformed uncertainty product. Such a route remains unavailable until its
owning process supplies an exact content-bound scientific authority and the
NOI method binds and satisfies the parity interface. It makes no implementation
conformity, validation, calibration, performance, readiness, or production
claim.
